Dependency grammar (DG) is a decription of language as having the dependency relation viewing [[selbri|main verb]] as the structural center of the whole clause structure. All other syntactic units (e.g. words) are either directly or indirectly dependent on the verb. DGs are distinct from [[Phrase structure grammar|phrase structure grammars]] (constituency grammars), since DGs lack phrasal nodes - although they acknowledge phrases. Structure is determined by the relation between a word (a head) and its dependents. Dependency structures are flatter than constituency structures in part because they lack a finite verb phrase constituent, and they are thus well suited for the analysis of languages with free word order, such as Czech and Turkish.
